The subject of the sentence "Any and every thought should be taken out and explored by whoever wishes, whenever they wish." is self-evidently "thoughts."

Had I meant to refer to something "more than talking or thinking," I would've used a different noun for the subject of the sentence.

To your example - let's take the thought "we should set a puppy on fire" out and explore it.

I see a reprehensible act with no possibility of any merit that causes significant harm to a living creature, and therefore an act in which I have absolutely no desire to engage, and an act that I in fact would try to prevent were to I to see someone else trying to engage in it.

That's a specific analysis of that specific act, and one that came about specifically because I took the idea out and explored it.

Had I just clanged shut the doors of my mind to the whole idea, I might well hold the same position regarding the act, but I'd really have no context for that position. It would be no more meaningful, really, than just nodding and going along with whatever somebody else says about something. I wouldn't hold the position because I analyzed things and arrived at it, but merely because I adopted it and shoved it into the appropriate space in my brain. And the danger there is that a position that's that easily adopted can be just as easily set aside, whenever it seems expedient to do so.
